relationships.subject: PRG-1
relationships.evidence_quote: PRG‐1 overexpression alleviates RNS‐induced mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia from Week 5 to Week 9, while PRG‐1 silencing exacerbated pain

relationships.subject: PRG-1
relationships.evidence_quote: These results demonstrated that hippocampal PRG‐1 alleviates RNS‐induced pain hypersensitivity and anxiety‐like behaviors.

relationships.subject: Neonatal repetitive noxious stimuli
relationships.evidence_quote: The western blots revealed a significantly reduced expression of hippocampal PSD protein‐95 (PSD95), a scaffold protein derived from the origin of postsynaptic compact regions, in RNS rats at 6 and 9 weeks

relationships.subject: PRG-1
relationships.evidence_quote: PRG‐1 overexpression fully restored PSD95 levels

relationships.subject: PRG-1
relationships.evidence_quote: PRG‐1 overexpression and ATPγS treatment significantly attenuated intracellular Ca2+ overload at 9 weeks in RNS rats

relationships.subject: Verapamil
relationships.evidence_quote: Hippocampus bilateral injection of verapamil (100 μM per day, P60–62), a kind of calcium channel blocker, attenuated RNS‐induced mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia

key_findings: Hippocampal PRG-1 relieves neonatal RNS-induced hyperalgesia and anxiety via stage-specific regulation of AMPAR GluR1/GluR2 and NMDAR GluN2A/GluN2B and synapse remodeling.
RNS reduces hippocampal PSD95, restored by PRG-1 overexpression; PRG-1 attenuates intracellular Ca2+ overload.
